algorithm.Title: Headache - Female (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Female
Definition: Headache assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for sudden maximal/severe headache, stroke signs, seizure, confusion, reduced consciousness, meningitis features, major head injury with deterioration, carbon-monoxide exposure, acute visual loss, or pregnancy/postpartum danger signs. Note the last-known-well time and do not give food, drink, aspirin, or unprescribed medicine when stroke, bleeding, or impaired swallowing is possible. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Has there been a seizure, numbness or weakness in the body or face, sudden extremely painful onset, difficulty speaking, balancing, walking, or remembering things, drowsiness or confusion, loss of vision, a non-fading rash, a very high temperature with a stiff neck or light sensitivity, or a recent major head injury with deterioration?
questions.Information: NHS.UK headache guidance lists these as emergency ambulance or Emergency Department criteria - possible stroke, meningitis, or other serious cause.

questions.Question: Did the headache occur after any head injury within the last 3 months, with none of the immediate life-threatening features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK directs headache after head injury within 3 months to 999 or Emergency Department. This branch preserves emergency assessment while avoiding an unsupported rule that every stable case requires a Qatar ambulance; exact local destination and transport remain local approval required.

questions.Question: Are there vision or eye problems, is the headache triggered or worsened by coughing, sneezing, bending down, or exercise, is there vomiting, is a child's headache getting worse or waking them at night, or is there jaw pain when eating or a tender scalp?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance lists these as reasons to seek urgent clinical review or get an urgent primary-care review.

questions.Question: Is this a mild-to-moderate headache with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends hydration, rest, and simple pain relief for uncomplicated headaches.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency headache response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for sudden maximal/severe headache, stroke signs, seizure, confusion, reduced consciousness, meningitis features, major head injury with deterioration, carbon-monoxide exposure, acute visual loss, or pregnancy/postpartum danger signs. Note the last-known-well time and do not give food, drink, aspirin, or unprescribed medicine when stroke, bleeding, or impaired swallowing is possible. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: worsening confusion; new weakness, numbness, speech, balance, or vision change; seizure, neck stiffness, rash, or reduced consciousness.

advice.Title: Emergency assessment after recent head injury
Content: Arrange prompt in-person emergency assessment through the Qatar governance-approved pathway and do not self-drive. Call 999 immediately if severe or worsening headache, repeated vomiting, seizure, weakness/numbness, speech/balance/vision change, confusion, drowsiness, collapse, abnormal breathing, or other deterioration develops. Exact destination and transport for a stable patient remain local approval required.
Call Back If: worsening headache or repeated vomiting; confusion, drowsiness, seizure, weakness, speech, balance, or vision change; collapse or abnormal breathing.

advice.Title: Urgent headache review
Content: Arrange same-day or next-day medical review through the approved Qatar pathway, especially for vision changes or persistent vomiting.
Call Back If: vision worsens; vomiting continues.

advice.Title: Governed care for a familiar uncomplicated headache
Content: Rest in a quiet environment, maintain usual fluids if not restricted, eat normally, and avoid alcohol and known triggers. Medicine choice/dose requires age, weight, pregnancy/breastfeeding, allergy, kidney/liver disease, ulcer/bleeding risk, anticoagulants, and current medicines under the approved Qatar pathway.
Call Back If: headache persists, changes, or worsens; new fever, neck stiffness, vomiting, vision, speech, weakness, seizure, or pregnancy/postpartum symptoms.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What is the person's exact age and sex, are they pregnant or within 6 weeks postpartum, when did the headache start and reach maximum severity, and is it first, worst, new, or different? Include trauma, fever, neurological/visual symptoms, anticoagulants, carbon monoxide, and safeguarding concerns.
